user_direction: User likes F03/F04 better and requests 10 additional variants. Direction approved for further exploration, no individual ship selected for modeling.

constraints.drum: fixed, fore-aft axis, no increased diameter/thickness/volume
constraints.baydoor: native rectangular dorsal lid translates aft and slightly up
constraints.wings: inner slide plus outer roll upward; forward sweep in flight

variants.brief: Rebuild the wing root as a long recessed oblique guide channel in the lower neck, with a nested closed rectangular carrier and a compact partly buried hinge at its outer end. The neck's lower contour rises toward the cockpit as one decisive shallow diagonal, creating a lean tapered wedge. One long red trapezoid repair inset follows this contour; a short three-vane vent sits aft of it. Thin forward-swept wings have a broad clipped outside corner and one recessed rectangular inner field. Inside the unchanged round drum outline, make a deep rounded-rectangle center pocket containing TWO unequal broad horizontal recesses, with a small flat olive repaired lower-quarter field. Do not add a protruding center cap.
variants.prompt:
Use case: precise-object-edit / spaceship design variant.
Create ONE NEW three-view concept variant of the RH pirate LIGHT FIGHTER based on image 1, the direction the user likes. Preserve its successful fore-aft-axis ROUND REAR DRUM and TWO compact engines. This is a controlled exploration of wing mounting, lean neck shape and CUT-IN drum-face design, not a new faction or class of ship.

INPUT ROLES:
Image 1 = accepted DESIGN DIRECTION F03 or F04; edit this three-view sheet into the specified new variant. Keep its perspective, layout, overall proportions, protected cabin and round-drum envelope.
Image 2 = actual ORIGINAL FIGHTER COCKPIT closeups. Mandatory geometry/identity anchor. The entire cockpit is unchanged.
Image 3 = actual original fighter flight reference, for original physical SIZE and wing proportions only. Its old sideways drum orientation and one-engine arrangement are intentionally superseded by image 1.
Image 4 = native BAYDOOR closed/open, showing separate rectangular top lid moving AFT and slightly UP.
Image 5 = native wing flight/mid/folded, motion constraint only; final sheet uses FLIGHT.

HARD INVARIANTS:
1. Keep the complete CABIN from image 1 untouched, matching actual module in image 2: identical size/position/outline, broad sloped blue front windshield, narrow black/yellow divider then continuous lower blue band, tall side panes and original broad metal frames, small original brow, opaque stepped chin with red side insert and lower blue corner slots, separate lower hazard bumper and short tapered bottom. Do not redraw it into a different cabin. No new glazing, changed nose curvature, wider jaw, truck windows, elite canopy or armour around cabin. New hull starts BEHIND this module.
2. Exactly ONE round fixed drum, SAME or slightly smaller diameter and thickness than image 1; do NOT enlarge it, move its outer perimeter outward, add another rim or inflate the hull. Its CYLINDER AXIS IS ALONG THE FUSELAGE nose-to-tail. The round face looks FORWARD/BACKWARD, NOT sideways. It appears as a THIN VERTICAL SLAB in SIDE and a SHORT WIDE CROSSWISE BAND in TOP. Top band width is about 1.9 cabin widths, still comfortably inside the wing span. The top projection must show the full drum DIAMETER across the ship. No circular side view, no narrow longitudinal top spine. Only internal face recesses/panel fields may change.
3. Exactly TWO small axial engines below/alongside drum, each about half cabin width, exhausts face aft. No central third exhaust. Keep engines stationary, compact and independent from wings.
4. Keep a light fighter's narrow neck and modest overall mass/length, same baseline scale as image 1. No cargo-body bulk, tall shoulders, heavy armour tower or oversized wings. Do not fill all negative space under the neck with extra hull.

MECHANICS / FORMS:
Create meaningful new neck and wing-mount silhouette per the variant brief. Distinct internal sliding wing carrier AND separate hinged outer section. Moving wings cannot be welded to fixed cover; a visible separation is essential. Fore-aft hinge axes allow outer tips to roll UP ~63 degrees; inner carrier retracts IN/UP/AFT. Hinge dimensions moderate, integral solid housings and closed-backed pockets, no long exposed supports. Keep room for sweep clear of engine/drum.
Wings fly DOWN/OUT in front, and sweep FORWARD in TOP: nose UP, wing tips UP-LEFT / UP-RIGHT from roots. Entire panels sweep toward the cockpit, not engine. SIDE nose RIGHT: wing projects down-RIGHT. Keep source-like compact span/chord, thin meaningful sections and clipped angular tips. No giant sharp blades, backward jet wings or upfolded flight wings.
Original rectangular dorsal baydoor remains CLOSED immediately behind cabin, original scale. It slides AFT and slightly UP through a clear central corridor into a pocket UNDER the elevated drum base, BETWEEN engines. No fixed block across its moving plane. Preserve cargo floor and walls. No rotation of drum, no propeller blades, no new belly hatch. No motion arrows.
Detail through subtractive geometry: deep inset service fields, cut-in grilles with a few broad vanes, diagonal plane changes, recessed guide cartridges and meaningful joints. Moderate detail density exactly like image 1, neither blank cubes nor greeble carpets. Piracy is pragmatic rough repair: two or three flush donor fields with nonmatching seams, muted red/olive replacement sections and restrained wear. Broad quiet metal surfaces between useful details.
NO decorative raised plates/ribs, geometric rivets, exposed tubes/hoses/cables/piston rods, external frames/trusses/braces/cages or floating rings. No demonic motifs, horns/claws/skulls, national flags/crosses, Corsair forms, freighter masses or built-in guns. New necessary closed bearing housings only, all other sculpting mainly into the hull.

VISUAL:
Same clean technical concept rendering as image 1: crisp geometry, controlled dimensional shading, light warm-gray paper, worn pale warm metal with restrained muted red/olive fields. Preserve cabin colors. Three coherent views of ONE design on ONE landscape sheet: large front-side 3/4 LEFT, SIDE / FLIGHT upper RIGHT nose RIGHT, TOP / FLIGHT lower RIGHT nose UP. Complete uncropped silhouettes, adequate spacing. All views must describe the new geometry, especially wing mounts and drum orientation. No extra views, environment or effects. Title as specified plus three view labels only.

SPECIFIC VARIANT F05:
Rebuild the wing root as a long recessed oblique guide channel in the lower neck, with a nested closed rectangular carrier and a compact partly buried hinge at its outer end. The neck's lower contour rises toward the cockpit as one decisive shallow diagonal, creating a lean tapered wedge. One long red trapezoid repair inset follows this contour; a short three-vane vent sits aft of it. Thin forward-swept wings have a broad clipped outside corner and one recessed rectangular inner field. Inside the unchanged round drum outline, make a deep rounded-rectangle center pocket containing TWO unequal broad horizontal recesses, with a small flat olive repaired lower-quarter field. Do not add a protruding center cap.
All three views must reflect this structural variation, not just recoloring. Preserve the exact cabin and external drum envelope from image 1.
Title exactly: RH PIRATE FIGHTER / F05

variants.brief: Make a compact TWO-STEP closed wing saddle at the aft-lower neck, immediately ahead of each engine. A recessed rectangular slide socket sits within the lower step and a modest fore-aft hinge at its end; all load-bearing structure solid, no bars. The neck has two short stepped lower-edge cuts rather than a long wedge. An oblique deep service field with four broad inset vent blades sits on the rear flank, a smaller red donor hatch forward. Wings slightly broad at inner segment, rectangular clipped outer tip with one shallow trailing notch. Within the unchanged round drum face carve TWO broad vertical capsule-shaped channels separated by a calm integral center plane and one low off-center rectangular access panel. Outer circle remains exact.
